title: Tilt
description: A tilt shot rotates the camera vertically around a fixed position, pitch on the horizontal axis, tripod planted. Height is revealed or hidden by angle, not by lifting the support.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Reveal height without traveling. A body from shoes to face, a building from door to roof, a dinosaur from ankle to skull: the facts are stacked on one vertical.
The feet do not move. A crane or a jib is the wrong tool only if you wanted parallax of a rising support.
If the foreground must slide as you climb, boom. If you only need to look up, tilt.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Tripod, fluid head, horizontal axis. Start and end on composed frames; do not overshoot into ceiling unless that is the gag.
A wide lens exaggerates vertical stretch; a longer lens keeps the stack calmer. Prompt: Tilt on [Subject], camera rotating on its horizontal axis, climbing or descending the world from a fixed point.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to reveal height from one stance: a statue, a tower, a person from ground to face. Do not tilt as a fake crane-up.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Tilt Up and Tilt Down name direction. A Crane Up physically lifts the camera, so rooftops and streets change in parallax.
A Pedestal Up raises the support on a column without pitching. A Pan is the horizontal cousin.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Jurassic Park tilts up bodies and gates to stack scale from a planted stance. Citizen Kane uses vertical swings and stacked compositions to turn height into power.
Grammar: rotation, not travel.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a crane-up. The tell: foreground sliding, the support rising, the person shrinking in a map.
The fix: lock the position, pitch only, and let height arrive as angle.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Tilt in film?
A tilt rotates the camera vertically from a fixed position. The tripod stays put; the frame climbs or drops to reveal height.
Tilt vs Crane Up
A tilt only changes angle. A crane physically moves the camera through space, so parallax appears and the map can change.
When should I use Tilt?
Use it to reveal height without traveling. Do not use it when you need the camera to climb and ease back over a city.
How do I prompt Tilt for AI image or video?
Write a planted tripod and a vertical rotation. Example: Tilt on [Subject], camera rotating on its horizontal axis, climbing or descending the world from a fixed point.
